newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Socialists blast minister who offended Jews.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Socialists blast minister who offended Jews.

text.p: Switzerland's biggest coalition party demanded on Saturday the resignation of Economics Minister Jean-Pascal Delamuraz for offending Jews by describing calls for Swiss restitution to Holocaust victims as "blackmail".

The executive board of the Social Democrats (SP), one of four parties in the centre-left coalition that has ruled since 1959, adopted by a 25-11 vote a resolution accusing Delamuraz of unleashing a wave of anti-Semitism and urging him to step down.

Delamuraz, a Radical Democrat (FDP), has since apologised for the remarks he made in a newspaper interview last month as he finished a one-year term in the rotating Swiss presidency. He said he based his comment on inaccurate information.

SP parliamentary deputies Jean-Nils de Dardel and Paul Rechsteiner said in their motion in Berne that Delamuraz's comments used "the worst anti-Semitic stereotype" and made expressing anti-Jewish sentiment nearly respectable.
Delamuraz made no immediate comment, but FDP party president Franz Steinegger described the resignation call to Swiss radio as a "dumb move that damages Switzerland".
The SP motion urged the cabinet to distance itself from Delamuraz's remarks, something it has refused so far to do.
Delamuraz's comments outraged Israeli politicians and world Jewish groups, prompting them to renew threats of a boycott against Swiss banks. The threats have since been dropped.

Berne politicians say it would be extremely unusual for the cabinet to chastise Delamuraz considering Switzerland's political culture, which emphasises consensus over confrontation as a way of holding the multi-ethnic country together.

It was also unlikely because of a perception in Berne that Delamuraz's views were shared by a lot of ordinary Swiss, many of whose letters to newspapers have scorned Jewish restitution efforts as a way of extorting money from wealthy Switzerland.

Groups led by the World Jewish Congress (WJC) say Swiss banks and government profited cynically from the Holocaust by sitting on accounts left ownerless by Jewish victims and by buying stolen gold from Nazi Germany during World War Two.
The government and leading businesses have agreed in principle to create a Holocaust memorial fund, but details have yet to be worked out.

The Social Democrats' move adds pressure on the cabinet, but the seven ministers -- two from the SP and the others from three conservative parties -- are basically autonomous and do not have to follow party appeals.
